outcome: The telescope conjecture — the last of Ravenel's conjectures — was disproved by Burklund, Hahn, Levy and Schlank, announced 6 June 2023 at a conference at Oxford and posted to arXiv on 26 October 2023, both before the frozen revision's date of 26 January 2024; nothing that happened inside the window changed this problem's mathematical status.

counterexample.object: The T(n+1)-localized algebraic K-theory of a K(n)-local E_n-algebra (built from the K(1)-local sphere and generalizations), shown not to be K(n+1)-local, for every height n ≥ 1 and every prime — an explicit counterexample separating telescopic (T(n)-local) from chromatic (K(n)-local) localizations.
counterexample.verified_how: Constructed via algebraic K-theory computations (using trace methods / topological cyclic homology techniques); the arXiv preprint has stood with a single version since 26 October 2023 and has been the subject of a dedicated Oberwolfach Arbeitsgemeinschaft (13–18 October 2024) working through the argument, and the authors received the 2026 Clay Research Award for the result.

summary: The Wikipedia bullet describes the telescope conjecture as 'the last of Ravenel's conjectures ... to be resolved,' and it was in fact resolved — but before the window opened. Burklund, Hahn, Levy and Schlank announced a disproof at a conference at Oxford on 6 June 2023 and posted the preprint 'K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture' to arXiv on 26 October 2023 (arXiv:2310.17459, single version, no later revisions), both dates before the frozen revision's 26 January 2024 timestamp. The disproof shows the conjecture is false at every height n≥2 (and, by later refinement discussed at the Oberwolfach meeting, at height 1 too) and every prime, via an explicit algebraic K-theory construction. Expert digestion of this pre-window result did continue inside the window — a dedicated Oberwolfach Arbeitsgemeinschaft ('Algebraic K-Theory and the Telescope Conjecture,' 13–18 October 2024) worked through the proof, and the authors received the 2026 Clay Research Award for it — but digestion of an already-announced, already-preprinted result is not a new event under §6.1's date rule (first public written argument), so status is `open_stale`, dated to the October 2023 preprint. I also found an open, unassigned GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#2192) proposing to formalize the conjecture/disproof in Lean; its own text states 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me' — but the issue is merely a cataloguing/task-listing action by an AI agent, not any mathematical content, and it remains unassigned with no formalization produced, so it does not constitute an event or AI-assisted mathematics under §6.2. I searched for arXiv preprints in 2024–2025 that might extend or revisit the specific Ravenel telescope conjecture in stable homotopy theory and found only work on variant/generalized telescope conjectures for different triangulated-category settings (noetherian path algebras, Azumaya algebras, general presentably symmetric monoidal ∞-categories) — these are related problems under §3.1 (different objects/hypotheses), not cases of this specific bullet, and none report any AI involvement. No AI system produced, checked, or otherwise touched the original disproof or its digestion; searches turned up nothing to suggest otherwise.
competing_reading: One could argue the conjecture's Wikipedia article status only became authoritative/settled-in-the-literature during the window (via the 2024 Oberwolfach workshop and the 2026 Clay Award, both of which postdate the frozen revision), and that 'resolved' status should be dated to when experts fully validated it rather than to the original preprint. But §6.3 is explicit that dating uses the first public written argument, not later journal publication or recognition, so I did not adopt this reading; it would not change the `open_stale` classification in any case, since even the later validation events predate no new mathematical content and the underlying disproof itself is pre-window.
what_would_settle_it: Confirmation (already essentially in hand) of whether the arXiv paper has since appeared in a journal, and whether any post-window paper revises or extends the K-theoretic counterexample construction itself (as opposed to studying analogous telescope conjectures in other categorical settings) would remove any residual doubt about whether all mathematical content is pre-window.
